title: RFID Wooden Card — FSC Hardwood Veneer
summary: Wooden NFC cards laminate FSC- or PEFC-certified hardwood veneer (birch, cherry, walnut, maple) over a thin inlay core carrying a standard ISO/IEC 14443 or 15693 chip. The grain aesthetic is the product story — every card is visually distinctive. And the substrate plugs into existing NFC reader and printer ecosystems exactly as PVC does. Right for hospitality room keys, wine-estate tasting-room cards, real-estate lead magnets and premium gift / welcome-kit programmes.
heroPoints: FSC / PEFC hardwood veneer (birch, cherry, walnut, maple) over NFC inlay core — every card carries a unique grain pattern.
NTAG21x / MIFARE Classic / MIFARE DESFire EV3 chip options — identical reader and printer compatibility to PVC cards.
Laser engraving and UV digital CMYK printing on grain — logos, vCards, loyalty QR and sequential numbers with no ink-on-ink hand-off issues.
imageAlt: FSC hardwood-veneer NFC card with natural grain and embedded ISO/IEC 14443 inlay

brief.label: Material — hardwood veneer options
items: Birch (pale, even grain — the neutral-canvas option), cherry (warm red-brown — hospitality and wine estates), walnut (dark chocolate grain — executive and luxury), maple (light cream-gold — retail and welcome-kit giveaways).
Oak, ash, bamboo (as the cross-over option — see the bamboo-specific page for FSC Moso details) and zebrawood available on bespoke order.
Species with CITES Appendix II restrictions (some Dalbergia rosewoods) are excluded from the catalogue — we do not supply them even on request.

brief.label: Certification and chain of custody
items: FSC (Forest Stewardship Council) Chain-of-Custody certified timber through FSC-CoC licensed suppliers; chain-of-custody documentation ships with every order.
PEFC (Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification) is the complementary European scheme accepted by most EU procurement frameworks.
EU Deforestation Regulation 2023/1115 (EUDR) due-diligence statements are supported via FSC / PEFC CoC for EU market placement.

brief.label: Card body construction
items: 0.76–0.84 mm ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 thickness sandwich: hardwood veneer top layer + RFID inlay core + hardwood veneer bottom layer.
Veneer thickness 0.25–0.35 mm per face; the core substrate carries the antenna and chip.
Water-based polyurethane adhesive (no solvent-based chemistry); clear protective top-coat finish in matte, silk or gloss.

brief.label: Embedded inlay — chip options
items: NTAG213 ({chip:nxp-ntag-213:user_bytes} bytes) / NTAG215 ({chip:nxp-ntag-215:user_bytes} bytes) / NTAG216 ({chip:nxp-ntag-216:user_bytes} bytes) for NFC Forum Type 2 vCard, URI and product-authentication payloads.
MIFARE Classic 1K for loyalty and legacy-access programmes; MIFARE DESFire EV3 AES-128 for authenticated hotel-key and access deployments.
ISO/IEC 15693 ICODE SLIX available for shelf-sweep / bulk-scan scenarios such as premium-product authentication cards.

brief.label: Radio transparency
items: Hardwood veneer is fully transparent to 13.56 MHz radio — no read-range penalty versus the same inlay in PVC.
Antenna tuning is adjusted for the wood substrate's dielectric constant; Proud Tek ships tuned inlays as standard.
Moisture-stabilised veneer avoids seasonal humidity effects on antenna resonance that could otherwise detune the inlay.

brief.label: Personalisation — laser engraving
items: CO2 laser at 10.6 μm wavelength produces permanent dark-brown marks by controlled carbonisation of the veneer surface — the canonical decoration method.
Engraving depth 0.05–0.15 mm; spot size 0.1–0.3 mm; typical throughput 300–600 cards per hour on a mid-power (60–80 W) laser.
Laser marking needs no ink, primer or post-processing — compatible with food-contact and allergen-sensitive hospitality settings.

brief.label: Personalisation — UV digital print
items: UV flatbed CMYK (Mimaki / Roland / Mutoh class) prints directly onto the veneer; grain shows through for a distinctive layered aesthetic.
White base layer under the CMYK when the design requires opaque colour blocks — otherwise the grain reads through the ink.
Spot-foil (rose-gold, copper, matte-black) and blind-deboss available for premium welcome-kit and executive-card treatments.

brief.label: Durability and protective finish
items: Protective clear coat (polyurethane or UV-cured acrylic) provides moisture and wear resistance for 2–4 year typical wallet life.
Not rated for laundry, marine or industrial wash environments — for those duty cycles, polycarbonate or UHF-on-metal form factors are the correct choice.
Grain aging is expected and part of the aesthetic; a protective finish slows but does not stop natural tonal change.

brief.label: Deployment archetypes
items: Boutique and eco-lodge hotel room keys — room-key substrate aligned with the property's LEED, BREEAM or Green Key certification narrative.
Wine-estate tasting-room and wine-club loyalty cards — the material story reinforces the agricultural-craft brand positioning.
Premium-brand welcome kits — luxury apparel, artisan food and spirits, direct-to-consumer beauty brands that ship a branded NFC card with the first unboxing.
Executive and architect studio business cards — veneer-card variant of the engraved-business-card SKU for lower-volume executive use.

brief.label: Environmental positioning
items: FSC / PEFC chain-of-custody hardwood is a managed-forestry product; carbon sequestered during tree growth offsets much of the card's embodied carbon footprint.
Veneer card body is biodegradable after inlay removal; the inlay (PET + copper + silicon) routes through standard WEEE e-waste channels.
Regrowth cycles are materially slower than Moso bamboo (30–80 years vs 3–5) — hardwood wins on grain aesthetic and luxury positioning, bamboo wins on fastest-renewable ESG narrative.

brief.label: Regulatory and compliance
items: EU RoHS 3 (Directive 2011/65/EU) and REACH SVHC compliant — water-based adhesive avoids SVHC plasticiser concerns inherent to PVC.
CPSIA (US) lead and phthalate consumer-safety limits met by default.
EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR, 2023/1115) applies to wood placed on the EU market — FSC / PEFC CoC evidence supports due-diligence statements.

brief.label: Reader and printer compatibility
items: Full compatibility with HID, Nedap, Suprema, Salto, Assa Abloy and Dormakaba reader ecosystems — chip-driven, not substrate-driven.
Card printers (Fargo, Zebra, Evolis) handle veneer cards with minor feed-roller adjustment for the 0.76–0.84 mm tolerance window.
Dye-sublimation printing is not recommended on veneer cards — laser engraving and UV digital print are the supported decoration paths.

sections.title: Why hardwood-veneer cards earn their place in premium programmes that bamboo and PVC do not quite fit
sections.intro: Hardwood veneer is not the fastest-renewable substrate — bamboo is. It is not the toughest — polycarbonate and metal are. What it is, is the substrate where grain carries the brand signal. When the programme is premium-brand welcome kit, wine-estate tasting room, boutique hotel key or executive business card, the unique-grain visual story is what sells the substrate.
paragraphs: The engineering is simple. A 0.25–0.35 mm hardwood veneer sandwich around a standard NFC inlay core produces a 0.76–0.84 mm ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 card body that prints, engraves, reads and files exactly as a PVC card does. The chip ecosystem (NTAG21x, MIFARE, DESFire EV3, ICODE SLIX) is unchanged; only the antenna tuning is adjusted for the wood substrate's dielectric constant.

The commercial choice between hardwood veneer and bamboo is a brand-narrative choice. Moso bamboo wins on the 3–5-year regrowth cycle that ESG teams want in their annual report. Hardwood veneer wins on grain aesthetic — every cherry, walnut and birch card is visually unique, which is exactly what luxury and premium programmes want. The reader, the inlay and the FSC / PEFC chain-of-custody discipline are shared.

dataHighlight.heading: Grain pattern as the commercial differentiator
dataHighlight.text: Hardwood veneer's premium-brand case rests on a non-quant property: every card looks different. Walnut board-to-board grain variation, cherry colour depth, birch knots and maple fleck marks mean a 500-card print run ships 500 visually unique cards. For welcome kits, executive business cards and wine-estate tasting-room cards that customers keep, that uniqueness is the commercial value — an unboxing moment that a PVC card cannot produce. The ecological story (FSC chain-of-custody, biodegradable card body, standard inlay reader compatibility) is the supporting evidence, not the lead.

sections.title: Proud Tek wooden NFC card — species, finish and inlay options
bullets: Wood species catalogue: birch, cherry, walnut, maple standard; oak, ash, zebrawood on bespoke order. CITES-restricted Dalbergia rosewoods excluded.
Card body: 0.76–0.84 mm ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 veneer sandwich with water-based polyurethane adhesive and RFID inlay core.
Inlay: NTAG213 / NTAG215 / NTAG216, MIFARE Classic 1K, MIFARE DESFire EV3 AES-128 or ISO/IEC 15693 ICODE SLIX — antenna tuned for wood substrate.
Finish: matte / silk / gloss polyurethane clear coat or UV-cured acrylic — the clear coat provides the 2–4 year wallet-carry durability envelope.
Decoration: CO2 laser engraving (50–80 W) at 300–600 cards/hour, UV flatbed CMYK digital print, spot-foil (rose-gold / copper / matte-black), blind-deboss.
MOQ 300 blank / 500 printed; lead time 10–14 business days from artwork approval; samples within 5 working days.

sections.title: Deployment archetypes — where hardwood-veneer cards sit
bullets: Boutique and eco-lodge hotel room keys — wood-key substrate aligned with the property's LEED / BREEAM / Green Key certification story.
Wine-estate tasting-room cards and wine-club loyalty cards — the material reinforces the agricultural-craft brand narrative at point of sale.
Premium-brand welcome-kit NFC cards — luxury apparel, artisan spirits and D2C beauty brands shipping a branded card with first-unboxing moment.
Executive and architect-studio business cards — the hardwood-veneer variant is more formal than bamboo and more bespoke than the engraved wooden business-card SKU.
Real-estate agent lead-magnet cards — high-end residential and commercial brokers issuing a tap-to-vCard veneer card as a standout leave-behind.

sections.title: Roadmap — wooden NFC cards from curiosity to established premium substrate

items.label: 2014 — early boutique-hotel pilots
items.text: First commercial wooden NFC hotel keys at boutique eco-lodges in Scandinavia and the Pacific Northwest; cherry and maple veneer builds.

items.label: 2018 — EU single-use plastics pressure
items.text: EU Single-Use Plastics Directive (2019/904) and a patchwork of municipal plastic bans start pushing hospitality brands to audit card substrates.

items.label: 2020 — SASB / GRI / TCFD supply-chain disclosure
items.text: Supply-chain material-choice becomes a reportable ESG line; hardwood veneer cards appear as an illustrative line item in annual reports.

items.label: 2022 — FSC timber premium-brand rollouts
items.text: Luxury brands and D2C beauty / spirits adopt FSC walnut and cherry veneer cards for welcome kits and collector-edition loyalty.

items.label: 2023 — EU Deforestation Regulation published
items.text: Regulation 2023/1115 (EUDR) takes form, requiring due-diligence for wood placed on the EU market. FSC / PEFC CoC becomes operationally mandatory.

items.label: 2024 — EUDR application date
items.text: EUDR operational from 30 December 2024 (extended to 30 December 2025 for large operators); veneer-card suppliers harden CoC documentation flows.

items.label: 2026 — Today
items.text: Hardwood-veneer NFC cards ship as a catalogue option across boutique hotels, wine estates, premium brands and executive business-card programmes. Cross-buyer reference experience on sustainable-hotel-key, premium-brand-giveaway, wine-estate-tasting-room, real-estate-lead-magnet and artisan-retail-packaging wooden-card programmes shows.

faq.question: Are wooden NFC cards as durable as PVC?
faq.answer: They are built for wallet carry, badge holder insertion and normal tap-to-read duty — 2–4 year typical life with the clear-coat finish. Wood is a natural material and shows wear over heavy use; for laundry, marine or industrial wash environments PVC or polycarbonate cards are the correct choice.

faq.question: Can wooden cards be printed with full-colour artwork?
faq.answer: Yes, via UV flatbed CMYK digital print. The natural wood grain shows through the print as part of the aesthetic. Designs that work with the grain look striking; for opaque colour blocks a white base layer is printed first. Laser engraving is the alternative for a no-ink, grain-into-the-wood branded look. Dye-sublimation is not recommended on wooden card stock.

faq.question: Is the timber FSC-certified? What about EUDR?
faq.answer: Yes. We source from FSC / PEFC Chain-of-Custody certified suppliers and ship CoC documentation with every order. This supports EU Deforestation Regulation 2023/1115 (EUDR) due-diligence statements and EcoVadis / ISO 14001 supply-chain reporting. Species under CITES Appendix II (some Dalbergia rosewoods) are excluded from the catalogue.

faq.question: How does a wooden card compare to bamboo?
faq.answer: Hardwood veneer wins on grain aesthetic — every card is visually unique. Bamboo wins on the 3–5-year regrowth cycle versus 30–80 years for hardwood, and on a slightly lower unit cost. Choice is narrative-driven: executive / luxury programmes gravitate to walnut or cherry veneer, fastest-renewable ESG stories gravitate to Moso bamboo. Reader and printer compatibility is identical.
